keyVerseText: And Shallum the son of Kore, the son of Ebiasaph, the son of Korah, and his brethren, of the house of his father, the Korahites, were over the work of the service, keepers of the gates of the tabernacle: and their fathers, being over the host of the LORD, were keepers of the entry. gates: Heb. thresholds
rootMeaning: The root of קוֹרֵא (Qôwrêʼ) derives from the Hebrew verb קָרָא (qârâʼ), which fundamentally means to call out, proclaim, or summon. As an active participle, Qôwrêʼ literally means "crier," indicating one who calls or summons others. This root sense of vocal proclamation or calling adds depth beyond a mere proper name, suggesting a role or identity connected to calling, announcing, or leading vocally.
usageInScripture: The word קוֹרֵא appears only three times in Scripture, consistently as a proper name referring to two Levites connected to temple service. Two occurrences translate simply as "of Kore," identifying lineage, while one is rendered "And Kore," marking narrative introduction. This limited but consistent usage highlights the word primarily as a personal name tied to Levitical families, rather than a common noun, yet its etymological sense as a "crier" underpins the identity of these individuals within their priestly roles.
theologicalSignificance: Understanding קוֹרֵא as rooted in the concept of calling or proclaiming enriches our appreciation of the Levites' sacred duties as God's appointed ministers. These individuals, descended from Kore, were entrusted with roles involving the service and guardianship of the tabernacle, symbolizing God's call to His people and the proclamation of His presence. The name itself reminds believers that ministry involves responding to God's summons and faithfully calling others to Him. This reflects the evangelical call to be messengers of God's Word, echoing the divine initiative to call and redeem humanity through Christ.
keyVerseReflection: 1 Chronicles 9:19 states, "And Shallum the son of Kore... were over the work of the service, keepers of the gates of the tabernacle." Here, the name Kore identifies a lineage tasked with sacred responsibilities, emphasizing their role as guardians at the threshold of God's dwelling. The word קוֹרֵא in this verse connects the family identity to their duty of 'calling' or 'proclaiming' God's presence by managing access to the holy place, symbolizing the spiritual calling believers have to stand watch and minister in God's service.
